Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

    [9, 8, 9, 9, 8, 9, 9, 8, 9]
]

print(f"Grid shape: {len(grid)}x{len(grid[0])}")
print(f"Unique values: {sorted(set(value for row in grid for value in row))}")

# Check horizontal repetition pattern
def check_repetition():
    rep_units = []
    for col in range(9):
        cols = [row[col] for row in grid]
        rep_units.append(cols)
    
    # Check if columns 0-2 == columns 3-5 == columns 6-8
    unit1 = tuple(rep_units[i] for i in range(3))
    unit2 = tuple(rep_units[i] for i in range(3, 6))
    unit3 = tuple(rep_units[i] for i in range(6, 9))
    print(f"Column 0-2 == 3-5? {unit1 == unit2}")
    print(f"Column 3-5 == 6-8? {unit2 == unit3}")
    print(f"All three identical? {unit1 == unit2 == unit3}")

check_repetition()

# Find which positions have non-9 values
non_nine_positions = [(r, c) for r in range(len(grid)) for c in range(len(grid[0])) if grid[r][c] != 9]
print(f"\nNon-9 cell count: {len(non_nine_positions)}")
for pos in non_nine_positions[:20]:
    print(pos)
